name: Kingdom of Osroene
native: Orhay (Urhay), the Aramaic name of Edessa

predecessors.name: Seleucid Empire
predecessors.text: the Edessa district the Abgarid kings ruled: infobox 'Preceded by the Seleucid Empire'

successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: 'the remaining territory incorporated into the Roman province of Osroene' when Caracalla deposed Abgar IX

rulers.name: Ma'nu VIII, son of Ma'nu (first tenure)
Abgar VIII the Great, son of Ma'nu
Abgar IX Severus, son of Abgar

ledger.x: 132 BC: the Abgarid kingdom of Osroene appears at Edessa.
By 95 BC: Osroene a Parthian vassal.
66/65 BC: Osroene leaves the Parthian sphere.
115: Trajan takes northern Mesopotamia and Abgar VII submits.
118: a Roman-backed king rules Osroene again.
118: a Roman-backed king rules Osroene again, a client of Hadrian's Empire.
123: the Abgarid dynasty is restored under Ma'nu VII.
165: Rome retakes Edessa and reinstalls Mannus.
165: Mannus (Ma'nu VIII) is reinstalled and Osroene is a Roman client again (the 161-166 page; the Mesopotamia page: Northern Mesopotamia, including Osroene, 'were left under local vassal rulers').
214: the client kingdom ends with Caracalla's annexation ('the remaining territory incorporated into the Roman province of Osroene'); see the loss and dissolve events.
214: Caracalla deposes Abgar IX and annexes Osroene.

wars.name: Crassus' invasion of Parthia
wars.outcome: Parthian victory at Carrhae (53 BC); Osroene's king Abgar II, 'an ally of the Roman general Marcus Licinius Crassus', died later that year.

wars.name: Trajan's Parthian campaign
wars.outcome: Osroene submitted in 115 as a Roman protectorate and lost its independence by 116; Hadrian's withdrawal left the Euphrates the frontier again.

wars.name: Roman-Parthian War of 161-166
wars.outcome: Roman victory with 'minor Roman gains in upper Mesopotamia'; Edessa reoccupied and Mannus reinstalled in 165; Nisibis stayed Roman.

wars.name: Roman-Parthian war of Septimius Severus
wars.outcome: Severus 'mounted an invasion of the kingdom and possibly annexed some of its territory' but 'allowed the Abgar VIII to retain his kingdom'; Rome kept northern Mesopotamia round Nisibis and Singara.

wars.name: Roman annexation of Osroene
wars.outcome: Caracalla deposed Abgar IX and the remaining territory became the Roman province of Osroene (214).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given on any page; the Euphrates loop on the north and west is a natural frontier and the eastern limit (Nisibis?) is uncertain.
